critical_finding: TOKEN SPAN ALIGNMENT IS FUNDAMENTALLY BROKEN
return_offsets_mapping_note: The QADataset.__getitem__ in run_experiment.py does NOT pass return_offsets_mapping=True to the tokenizer. This causes encoding.get('offset_mapping') to return None, triggering the fallback heuristic.
fallback_heuristic: start_token = min(ans_start_char, len(ctx_ids) - 1); end_token = min(ans_end_char - 1, len(ctx_ids) - 1). This uses CHARACTER offsets as TOKEN indices, which is fundamentally wrong.
decode_mismatch_causes: Subword tokenization splits numbers (e.g., '2.5 amps' -> '2. 5 amps')
Multi-word answers span multiple subword tokens with different text boundaries
impact: With the broken heuristic, 99.3% of training examples receive WRONG start/end position labels. The model is trained to predict arbitrary token positions instead of the correct answer spans. This is the PRIMARY ROOT CAUSE of A1/A2 training collapse.
even_with_correct_alignment: Only 28.4% would decode to exact answer text. The remaining 67% would have token-aligned spans that decode to slightly different text (subword boundaries). This secondary issue would still limit but not prevent learning.
